pages.text: Line the [[whole]] up with 100%. On a 50 m drum of cable, 20 m of it fills 20 ÷ 50 = 0.4 of the bar. That is 40 hundredths, so 40%.

pages.name: Slide it there
pages.task: Of a 40 m cable run, 30 m is pulled in. Slide the marker to that percentage.
pages.why: The whole run, 40 m, lines up with 100%. 30 ÷ 40 = 0.75, which is 75 hundredths, so 30 m is 75% of the run.

pages.name: Part ÷ whole × 100
pages.text: The rule is part ÷ whole × 100. So a 9 V drop on 230 V is about 3.9%. Close up, 1% is 2.3 V, and 9 V lands just under 4%.

pages.name: Times by 100
pages.task: A calculator gives 6 ÷ 230 = 0.0260869…, about 0.026. What percentage is a 6 V drop on 230 V?
pages.why: 6 ÷ 230, about 0.026, is the share as a decimal, 26 thousandths. Times by 100 to count it in hundredths, 2.6%. Close up, 1% of 230 V is 2.3 V, and 6 V is between two and three of those.

pages.task: An order comes to £200. £50 of it is cable and the rest is fittings. What percentage of the order is cable?
pages.why: The whole is the £200 order and the cable is the part. 50 ÷ 200 = 0.25, so 25%. Dividing by the £150 of fittings would compare the cable with only the rest.
